newsitem.title: ITALY: Thousands protest in Rome against Italian budget.
newsitem.headline: Thousands protest in Rome against Italian budget.

text.p: Thousands of Italians marched through central Rome on Saturday to demonstrate against the centre-left government's 1997 austerity budget.
Police said there around 10,000 people gathered while organisers said up to 70,000 people took part in the march against Prime Minister Romano Prodi's budget.
Prodi has dubbed the budget Italy's last hope for inclusion among the founder nations of a single European currency. The budget aims to shave 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's deficit.

"Die for Maastricht? No, thanks," ran one protester's banner, referring to the tough economic requirements laid down in the Maastricht treaty as conditions for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"No to the Prodi government's budget, to taxes for Europe and taxes on homes," ran another banner.
The budget is a mix of spending cuts and tax hikes, including a so-called "Euro Tax", which the government hopes will help Italy qualify for the planned launch of EMU in 1999.
The package is currently being discussed by parliament and has to be ratified by the end of the year.
The march was organised by Cobas, a group that brings together small, independent trades unions from across Italy which do not adhere to the country's three main trades union confederations.
"This budget will cost Italy 90,000 jobs," Cobas spokesman Piero Bernocchi told reporters.
"This government is like the previous one: it fails to protect either workers or pensioners," he said, adding that the budget would force both groups to pay more taxes.
